description:
Implement PR 2 of the attachment-delivery stack: shared capability-driven BO file settings and a shared Channels resolver for TransportRequirements.

Workspace and stack
- Work in ../zaq-feat-channel-file-settings on feat/channel-file-settings, based on feat/email-capabilities at 19e8e7525. PR base is feat/email-capabilities while PR 1 is unmerged.
- Issue zaq-h2i.1 source and tests have already been moved into this worktree as uncommitted files. Preserve their struct fields, defaults, enforced keys, and existing test expectations. Do not recreate or overwrite them.
- Build on zaq-h2i.2 email capability alignment. Its implementation is in the branch base; verify current dependency state without waiting for PR 1 to merge merely to develop the stacked PR.
- Environment setup is incomplete: dev.secret.exs was copied and remains ignored; .claude/settings.local.json was absent and mix setup was not run. Verify branch-isolated database configuration and required dependencies before running setup/tests. Do not expose secrets or change user-level configuration without authorization.

Functional specifications
1. Add one shared File delivery section under Advanced settings to applicable connection forms, including SMTP. Reuse the existing capability snapshot endpoint and shared BO components. Visibility and behavior must follow capabilities, never provider-name cases in shared consumers.
2. Include maximum file size, maximum encoded message size (body, headers, encoded attachments), maximum attachments per message, and send message if files fail. Inspect all corresponding settings in ../zaq-feat-channel-files as reference only. Share labels, help text, defaults, normalization, validation, and storage semantics across forms.
3. Display fixed transport limits read-only. Show configurable limits as inputs with known transport ceilings enforced. Mark required configuration explicitly. Blank optional overrides use transport-provided limits; absent limits remain unresolved, never implicitly unlimited. Distinguish unsupported, unresolved, and explicitly not-applicable values. Display decimal MB (1000000 bytes) and persist integer bytes; counts are positive integers. Show field-local errors, save with the connection form, and preserve unrelated settings. Hide the section when no applicable controls or limit information exist.
4. Implement one shared resolver in the Channels domain that derives the existing TransportRequirements struct from adapter capabilities and the selected connection configuration. Bridges must not independently construct requirements or duplicate limit/default/policy rules. BO persists configuration values only, not the derived struct. Keep policy supplied by channel configuration separate from adapter transport capability facts.
5. Consumers must share the capability semantics and validation rules used for BO settings. If BO validates or previews effective requirements through the resolver, use the existing supported NodeRouter/Event boundary; do not add an endpoint without establishing a concrete consumer need.

Resolver lifecycle and exclusions
- The later delivery integration resolves requirements after selecting the actual outbound connection, before acquiring attachment bytes or planning delivery. For replies originating from IMAP, use the selected SMTP connection, not the IMAP configuration.
- Resolve once per delivery attempt and pass that result through preparation and execution. A later attempt resolves again against current inputs.
- This PR implements and tests the resolver but does not wire attachment acquisition, batching/planning, sending, execution, or history. The final stacked-PR objective remains sending attachments through EmailBridge and JidoChatBridge to their adapters.

Required design/discovery before coding
- Inspect the existing capability contract, adapter declarations, Channels APIs, Engine connection-settings operations, ChannelConfig validation, ConnectorConfig helpers, and BO forms/components. Record exact owning modules and files after discovery.
- Define the shared metadata needed for fixed/configurable constraints and required/optional configuration; agree on field keys/defaults and resolver API, result/error contract, unit conversion precision, and precedence rules before implementation. Fixed provider ceilings cannot be raised by configuration.
- Preserve existing Jido/Mattermost capability meanings. Do not change their unrelated declarations, adapters, or tests. If necessary configuration capability metadata is missing, document the gap and propose the smallest extension or dependency revision as an explicit prerequisite before making that change. No provider-name workaround and no invented attachment support just to display settings. Distinguish configuration capabilities from completed sending support.
- Follow the repository architectural approval rules for any uncovered contract changes. This issue is ready for discovery, not permission to invent an incompatible shared schema.

Action reuse assessment
- Extend/reuse the existing capability snapshot endpoint, Engine persistence operations, ChannelConfig validation, ConnectorConfig projections, and shared BO controls where their contracts fit. Record concrete candidates, owning modules, reuse/extend/local-only decisions, inputs/outputs/errors, side effects, and runtime dependencies before coding.
- The requirements resolver is a derived domain operation; assess whether it belongs as a pure local domain function or an existing operation extension. Do not create an Action, public endpoint, or agent tool solely for discoverability. Track any genuinely missing composable operation as a prerequisite under docs/action-reuse.md.
- All BO cross-service operations use NodeRouter with Zaq.Event. Keep selected connection identity and existing authorization boundaries intact.

Tests to add before implementation
- Use TDD with original tests; no copied old-worktree tests. Confirm expected red failures, then implement and verify green.
- Cover equivalent capability combinations across channel and SMTP forms; native/fallback/unsupported support; fixed/configurable and required/optional limits; blank and malformed input; exact MB-to-byte conversion; save/reload; preservation of unrelated settings; field-local errors; and unavailable capabilities without silently treating them as unlimited.
- Resolver tests cover known limits, valid configured values, precedence/ceiling violations, missing required constraints, not-applicable constraints, transfer modes, thread/edit support, policy defaults/explicit values, and deterministic results without file acquisition or send effects.
- Use property tests for numeric normalization, broad input spaces, and ceiling invariants. Keep real internal boundaries and use mocks only for external edges where needed. Preserve issue 1 tests and obtain approval before changing existing test behavior.
- Assess feature E2E need and create/wire the human UX approval and consolidated E2E prerequisites before implementation where required; defer authoring until approval.

Documentation and validation
- Update relevant Channels/configuration documentation and focused module/API documentation with actual ownership, capability semantics, persisted units/defaults, and resolver errors; avoid duplicating policy documents.
- Follow AGENTS.md, docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md, docs/action-reuse.md, docs/services/channels.md, docs/services/system-config.md, DESIGN.md, docs/bo-components.md, and docs/testing-approach.md. Refine durable steps in Beadwork and validate prerequisite edges before coding.
- Run required issue-level checks and targeted tests. Do not restart mix precommit without authorization; record it as a remaining final gate. No commit, push, or PR publication without authorization. Record design decisions, tests, remaining gates, and adapter prerequisites in this issue.
title: [zaq-h2i.3] Add shared file settings and capability-driven transport requirements
